history.dynasty: Unknown - early shrine; temple complex attributed to Garhwal rulers
history.period: Ancient (Puranic); masonry structure medieval or later (exact construction date uncertain)
history.summary: Revered Shakti Peetha on Surkut mountain at about 2,756 m, where Sati's head ('sir') is believed to have fallen - 'Surkanda' from 'Sirkhanda'. Exact construction date is uncertain; one source attributes the built structure to the Parmar-era Garhwal rulers (8th-12th c. CE), unverified. Local discovery legend credits Anand Singh Jardhari of Jardhar village. Reached by a 2-3 km uphill trek from Kaddukhal. CSV town 'Tehri' is wrong - the temple is near Dhanaulti (about 8 km), not Tehri town; corrected to Dhanaulti. CSV 'state' column holds town names - corrected to Uttarakhand.

name: Surkanda Devi Temple
town_description: Dhanaulti is a quiet Himalayan hill station in Tehri Garhwal, about 25 km from Mussoorie, known for deodar forests, mountain views and its proximity to Kanatal.

travel.road: About 8 km from Dhanaulti and 33 km from Mussoorie; a 2-3 km uphill trek from Kaddukhal village where vehicles are parked.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Ganga Dussehra (May-June) draws large crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Summer 5 AM to 7 PM, winter 7 AM to 5 PM (verify before visiting).
